hints: Ignore the direction change for a moment: can you already produce the rows in normal left-to-right order?

Do a normal level-order BFS and keep a boolean leftToRight that flips after every row. On reversed rows, either reverse the finished row or insert each value at the front (a LinkedList makes that O(1)).

1. If root is null return an empty list.
  2. BFS with a queue; read size at the start of each row.
  3. Pop size nodes, pushing children left then right as usual.
  4. Add each value at the end if leftToRight, else at the front of the row.
  5. Save the row and flip leftToRight.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: For each depth, collect its nodes with a separate DFS and reverse the odd depths.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Single BFS by levels; build odd rows by adding to the front of a linked list so no extra reversal pass is needed.

explain: For [5,2,7,1,3,6,9], row 0 is read left to right: [5]. Row 1 pops 2 then 7 but inserts at the front, giving [7,2]. Row 2 is left to right again: [1,3,6,9]. The queue order itself never changes, only how values are placed into each row, which keeps the BFS simple. Edge case: an empty tree returns [].
recognize: 'Row by row but alternate direction each level' → level-order BFS plus a direction flag.
